toBuy.note: Shrimp, squid, and clams. Half a bag is plenty for this.

fromThePantry.note: Worth the trip. It coats the grains and makes the whole thing richer.

tools.name: Frying pan (about 24 cm)
tools.note: Everything happens here, in three passes.

tools.name: Spatula
tools.note: For pressing the rice flat, not just stirring.

tools.name: Knife
tools.note: The carrot and onion need to be cut small.

tools.name: Cutting board
tools.note: A clean plate can stand in.

tools.name: Microwave
tools.note: For the packed rice. 2 minutes at 500 to 600 W.

tools.name: Plate
tools.note: To park the cooked seafood while the vegetables fry.

steps.title: Dice the carrot and onion small
steps.text: Cut both into pieces about 5 mm across, roughly the size of the shrimp in the mix.
steps.hint: Fried rice cooks fast. Anything bigger than 5 mm will still be crunchy when the rice is done.

steps.title: Microwave the rice for 2 minutes
steps.text: Heat both packs, then open them and let the steam escape while you cook. Slightly dry rice fries better than fresh, moist rice.

steps.title: Cook the seafood first and take it out
steps.text: Melt 1 tbsp of butter over medium-high heat, add the seafood straight from frozen, and cook for 3 minutes until the shrimp turn opaque. Move it to a plate and leave the liquid in the pan.
steps.hint: This is the step that decides whether the fried rice is soggy. Frozen seafood dumps a lot of water, and you want that water out of the pan before the rice goes in.

steps.title: Boil off the liquid, then fry the vegetables
steps.text: Let the liquid in the pan bubble away for about a minute until the pan is nearly dry. Add the remaining 1 tbsp of butter, the carrot, the onion, and the garlic if using, and fry for 3 minutes until the onion turns translucent.
steps.hint: Keep the heat at medium once the butter goes in. Butter burns and turns bitter over high heat.

steps.title: Add the rice and press it flat
steps.text: If you're using the egg, push the vegetables to one side, crack it into the bare half of the pan, and scramble it loosely for 20 seconds. Add the rice, break up the lumps, and mix until every grain is coated. Then press it flat with the spatula and leave it for a minute so the bottom toasts. Turn it over and press again.
steps.hint: Pressing, not constant stirring, is what makes the crispy bits. Add the rice while the egg is still wet and it will coat the grains instead of forming lumps.

steps.title: Season at the edge and fold the seafood back in
steps.text: Pour the soy sauce onto the bare metal around the edge so it scorches for a second, then stir it through. Return the seafood, season with salt and pepper, and toss for 30 seconds. Serve straight away.
steps.hint: The seafood only goes back at the end. Squid that gets fried twice turns rubbery.

troubleshooting.solution: The seafood liquid stayed in the pan, or the rice was still steaming. Press the rice flat over medium heat for an extra minute or two per side to drive the moisture off.
Break the lumps with the edge of the spatula rather than folding them. A little extra butter helps the grains separate.
It cooked too long. Three minutes in the first pass and 30 seconds at the end is the whole budget.
Add another 1/2 tsp of soy sauce scorched at the edge of the pan, and be generous with the black pepper. Butter needs more salt than oil does.
Bacon or canned tuna both work, and so does a second egg. For tuna, drain it well and add it with the rice rather than frying it first.
